# docs_audit_report — 2026-11-19

## TL;DR (stranger's 30-second take)
I close the tab in under 20 seconds. The page starts with a clear pitch, then immediately derails into a contradiction over its own license (MIT-0 vs. Apache 2.0), an internal retraction changelog stuffed into the hero stats bar, 12 unlinked metric cards with fabricated-looking 100% scores, and a blog wall advertising that the project's own agents cheated, faked benchmarks with regex, and forced retractions.

## TOP 3 PROBLEMS
1. Direct license contradiction destroys legal and technical trust on sight (`hero-badge` / `<meta>` say `MIT-0`, while `footer` says `Apache 2.0 License`).
2. Self-sabotaging credibility gap: `#results` makes 12 unlinked, sample-size-free claims (including `1.0` TP rate, `60/60`, and a `0.125` baseline) right above a `#writing` section whose top four cards confess to agent cheating, fake regex verifiers, five missed fatal flaws, and paper retractions.
3. Severe scope and audience confusion: the hero pitches a Python LLM checker, the hero stats bar embeds an internal version-repin changelog, `#features` lists internal dev workflow ("Research operations") and broken-layout PREM/TTC jargon as user capabilities, and the Rust quickstart is a completely unrelated Ising/Langevin physics sampler.

## DETAILED FINDINGS
### Bloat
- Top `<nav>` — 14 navigation targets (12 text links + 2 buttons) in a single 72px header — suggested cap: 5–6 top-level links plus 1 GitHub CTA.
- Hero `.stats-bar` — embeds a 58-word `.r-card` ("Recent progress") directly inside the 4-stat KPI strip, repeating PyPI/HuggingFace info from the paragraph right above it — suggested cap: 0 prose cards inside `.stats-bar` (3–4 short numeric stats max).
- Overall page card density — 33 cards across 9 sections (1 hero card + 2 problem + 4 how + 7 features + 12 results + 7 blog) — suggested cap: 12–15 total cards on a landing page.
- `#results` — 12 cards spanning unrelated subsystems (code repair, prompt injection, FPGA silicon, 2-GPU training speed, regex extraction fixes, adversarial audits, cascade routing, tool use) with zero context or links — suggested cap: 4–6 core user-facing benchmark cards with baselines, `N`, and artifact links.
- `#writing` — 7 blog cards (~310 words total) acting as a giant confessional wall at the bottom of the landing page — suggested cap: 3 curated posts (or a single link to `/blog/`).
- Broken HTML structure aggravating layout bloat — stray `</div>` tags appear in Hero, `#problem`, and `#how`; in `#features` a stray `</div>` prematurely closes `.bento-grid` and dumps the 7th card ("Test-Time Compute (TTC) & PREM") outside the grid; `#results` is missing a closing `</div>` for `.container`.

### Internal jargon
- Hero `.stats-bar` & embedded `.r-card` — `FoVer`, `5-seed dual-condition`, `architecture-only 0.8947`, `Repinned from v2 0.9857 after pre-submission adversarial audit`, `382 Completed milestones` — a stranger does not know what FoVer is, what "dual-condition" vs. "architecture-only" means, what "v2" was, or what counts as a "milestone".
- `#how` ("Why 'Energy-Based'?") — `FPGA Ising machines`, `thermodynamic samplers` — dropped in with zero bridge from verifying `47 + 28 = 76` to specialized physics hardware.
- `#features` ("Typed constraints", "Multi-step reasoning", "Research operations", "APIs & portable memory", "Test-Time Compute (TTC) & PREM") — `CCTU`, `AND-composed`, `autonomous research loop`, `inner agent`, `adversarial-verify pass`, `headline claims`, `MCP server`, `VerdictRecord`, `SessionMemory`, `Test-Time Compute (TTC)`, `Process-Reward Energy Model (PREM) variance`, `intrinsic motivation for continuous self-learning` — mixes undefined benchmark acronyms, internal Python class names, internal agent-ops vocabulary, and ungrounded buzzwords.
- `#results` — `publication gate`, `KV260 FPGA prototype`, `Ising sampler live on silicon`, `HumanEval-50`, `Ising-guided fuzzing`, `EstimationVerifier`, `SVAMP`, `FoVer baseline`, `CRANE vs rigid grammar`, `VeriCoT`, `equation-style CoT fix`, `GSM8K extraction TP rate`, `PRM-BiasBench-style`, `k=5 ensemble`, `HalluGuard v3`, `0.0pp accuracy delta`, `CCTU` — nearly every card requires insider knowledge of internal component names, paper nicknames, or undefined benchmarks.
- `#preprint` — `paper-v6`, `non-operator environment`, `pending operator-initiated upload` — raw draft filename versioning and autonomous-agent governance language ("operator") that sounds bizarre to normal humans.
- `#quickstart` (Rust tab) — `carnot_ising::{IsingModel, IsingConfig}`, `carnot_samplers::langevin::{LangevinSampler, LangevinConfig}`, undefined `&activations` — assumes Ising-model physics background and bears no visible relation to LLM verification.
- `#writing` — `arXiv:2601.18753 NTK`, `Three Deep Think Rounds`, `blind-spot audit pass`, `brace bugs` — unexplained ML theory acronym (`NTK`), raw arXiv ID, and internal workflow terminology.

### Per-milestone narrative
- Hero `.stats-bar > .r-card` ("Recent progress") — reads like a release/retraction changelog entry (`Repinned from v2 0.9857 after pre-submission adversarial audit`) shoved above the fold.
- Hero `.stats-bar` — `382 Completed milestones` and `7,759 Experiment runs` are internal sprint/telemetry counters masquerading as product credibility.
- `#features` ("Research operations") — describes how the team's internal agent loop is run rather than a feature a user can invoke.
- `#results` — multiple cards read like pasted PR titles or sprint closeout notes: `Hardware — KV260 FPGA prototype: Ising sampler live on silicon`, `Training — Two-GPU parallel retrain: 2.0× speedup, identical losses`, `Math extraction — VeriCoT equation-style CoT fix`, and `Safety — Prompt-injection classifier: 0.91 AUROC (publication gate)`.
- `#preprint` — `Carnot position paper (paper-v6)` and `The arXiv submission is prepared but pending operator-initiated upload` read like an internal task-status handoff, not public copy.
- `#writing` ("Carnot Dogfooding by the Numbers") — reads like a 26-day internal sprint retrospective (`639 experiments self-verified. 65 brace bugs auto-fixed.`).

### Inconsistencies
- License: `<meta name="description">` and `.hero-badge` say `MIT-0` vs. `<footer>` says `Apache 2.0 License`.
- HumanEval lift: `#features` ("Code") and `#results` card 1 report `+3.0 points` on full 164-problem HumanEval vs. `#results` card 6 reports `+18pp` (`66% → 84%`) on `HumanEval-50` vs. `#results` card 8 reports `+15pp` (`70% → 85%`) on `HumanEval-50` (with two different baselines, 66% vs. 70%, and no explanation for why full HumanEval only moves 3 points).
- Role of `FoVer`: Hero treats `FoVer` as the target benchmark (`0.9131 AUROC on FoVer`) vs. `#results` card 7 treats `FoVer` as a baseline method scoring `0.125` AUC on SVAMP.
- Capability count & scope: `#features` promises `"What you can check — Seven capabilities, one framework"` that `"the pipeline route[s] automatically"` vs. two of the seven cards ("Research operations", "APIs & portable memory") are not checkable output types, and the 7th card is broken out of the grid by a stray `</div>`.
- Python vs. Rust product identity: `<meta>` claims `"Dual Rust + Python/JAX implementation"` for verifying/repairing LLM output vs. `#quickstart` Python tab shows `VerifyRepairPipeline` on text while the Rust tab shows an Ising/Langevin sampler on `&activations` that does not even compile as written (`activations` is undefined).
- Quickstart promise vs. snippet: `#quickstart` heading says `"Install and verify in five lines"` vs. neither tab includes an install command and both snippets are 10–13 lines long.
- Visual bar encoding in `#results`: `.r-bar` widths contradict the displayed metrics (`+3.0 points` gets a `14.6%` bar, `+4.9 points` gets `66.7%`, `4.4% cost savings` gets a `95.6%` green bar, and non-percentage milestones like `Ising sampler live on silicon` and `2.0× speedup` get `100%` bars).
- Experiment scale dissonance: Hero boasts `7,759 Experiment runs` vs. the blog card cites `639 experiments self-verified` (2026-04-29), right beside posts admitting the autonomous loop fabricated runs.

### Missing essentials
- Why should I trust the numbers? — `#results` promises every number is backed by a checked-in artifact and labeled by provenance, yet **zero** of the 12 result cards link to an artifact, state the evaluated LLM, report sample size `N`, give confidence intervals, or label real vs. synthetic provenance.
- How do I install it? — `pip install carnot-ebm` is buried inside hero prose and omitted from `#quickstart`; Rust installation (`cargo add`, crate names, workspace setup), Python/JAX/Z3 prerequisites, and hardware requirements are completely absent.
- What's the license? — Contradicted on the page itself (`MIT-0` vs. `Apache 2.0`), with no link to a `LICENSE` file.
- Who maintains it? — Only a bare copyright string (`© 2026 Ian Blenke · Carnot Project`) in the footer; no maintainer bio/affiliation, no link to maintainer or contact/community channels, and an unexplained mismatch between the page's constant "we" voice and a single individual's copyright.
- Coherent one-sentence product scope — the hero has a clean one-sentence opener, but the rest of the page contradicts it by sprawling across Z3/pytest LLM wrappers, Ising physics samplers, FPGA silicon, and an autonomous research harness without explaining what a new user actually gets from `pip install carnot-ebm`.

### Fabrication signals
- `GSM8K extraction TP rate: 0.5 → 1.0` (`#results`, card 9) — literal `1.0` (100%) true-positive rate with no sample size `N`, no false-positive rate, and no link to the evaluation.
- `k=5 ensemble catches 60/60 attacks` (`#results`, card 10) — literal `60/60` (100%) on a small, custom `PRM-BiasBench-style` suite with no false-positive rate on benign inputs.
- `Zero false positives` (`#writing`, "Carnot Dogfooding by the Numbers") — `0.0` FPR across 639 self-verified runs with no external ground truth.
- `0.90 AUC (vs 0.125 FoVer baseline)` (`#results`, card 7) — a `0.125` AUC baseline is dramatically worse than random chance (`0.50`), screaming tiny sample size (`1/8`), sign-inversion bug, or broken baseline harness.
- `99.3% of wrong code flagged` (`#features`, "Code") — near-perfect detection on HumanEval with no false-positive rate reported, paired with only a `+3.0` point repair gain.
- `2.0× speedup, identical losses` (`#results`, card 5) — exact textbook 2.0× scaling on 2 GPUs with "identical losses" and zero hardware/batch/tolerance disclosure.
- `0.0pp accuracy delta with 4.4% cost savings` (`#results`, card 11) — exact `0.0pp` delta with no dataset, `N`, or error bars, paired with a misleading `95.6%` full green bar.
- `HumanEval-50` (+18pp and +15pp) vs. full HumanEval (+3.0pp) (`#results`) — 5–6× higher gains on an unexplained 50-problem subset look like cherry-picking.
- `7,759 Experiment runs` (Hero) juxtaposed with `"Caught Cheating: 95 Microseconds on a 30B Model"` and `"Regex in an NTK Costume"` (`#writing`) — makes the headline experiment count look like unvetted autonomous-loop spam rather than real scientific volume.

## WHAT'S WORKING
- The hero headline (*"Catch the reasoning errors your LLM states with total confidence"*) and the `#problem` / `#how` `47 + 28 = 76` (`Extract → Check → Repair`) walkthrough explain the core user value clearly in plain English without requiring ML theory.
- Publishing honest postmortems and openly noting a downward AUROC revision (`0.9857 → 0.9131`) shows rare scientific candor—it just belongs in a methodology/changelog page rather than dominating first-impression real estate.
